import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

class LegacyModel:
    def __init__(self):
        self.woe_tabs = None
        self.coef_ = None

    def fit(self, frame: pd.DataFrame, train_rows: np.ndarray | None = None) -> "LegacyModel":
        if train_rows is not None:
            frame = frame[frame[".row"].isin(train_rows)]

        frame["bad"] = np.where(frame["creditability"] == "bad", 1, 0)

        # Binning functions
        def bin_duration(x):
            return pd.cut(x, bins=[-np.inf, 12, 24, 36, np.inf], right=False,
                           labels=["lt12", "12-24", "24-36", "36+"])

        def bin_amount(x):
            x[np.isnan(x)] = 0  # missing amount = 0
            return pd.cut(x, bins=[-np.inf, 1400, 4000, 8000, np.inf], right=False,
                           labels=["lt1400", "1400-4000", "4000-8000", "8000+"])

        # Create bins
        frame["checking"] = frame["status.of.existing.checking.account"]
        frame["duration"] = bin_duration(frame["duration.in.month"])
        frame["history"] = frame["credit.history"]
        frame["purpose"] = frame["purpose"]
        frame["amount"] = bin_amount(frame["credit.amount"])
        frame["savings"] = frame["savings.account.and.bonds"]
        frame["employment"] = frame["present.employment.since"]
        frame["instalment"] = frame["installment.rate.in.percentage.of.disposable.income"]

        vars = ["checking", "duration", "history", "purpose", "amount", "savings", "employment", "instalment"]

        # Calculate WoE
        G = np.sum(frame["bad"] == 0)
        B = np.sum(frame["bad"] == 1)
        self.woe_tabs = {}

        for v in vars:
            lv = np.sort(frame[v].unique())
            ng = [np.sum((frame[v] == l) & (frame["bad"] == 0)) for l in lv]
            nb = [np.sum((frame[v] == l) & (frame["bad"] == 1)) for l in lv]
            w = np.log((np.array(nb) + 0.5) / B / (np.array(ng) + 0.5) * G)
            self.woe_tabs[v] = pd.DataFrame({"var": v, "bin": lv, "n_good": ng, "n_bad": nb, "woe": w})

        # Apply WoE
        X = pd.DataFrame(index=frame.index)
        for v in vars:
            t = self.woe_tabs[v]
            X[f"woe_{v}"] = t["woe"].reindex(frame[v]).values  # unseen level -> NA

        X["bad"] = frame["bad"]
        y = X["bad"]
        X = X.drop(columns=["bad"])

        # Fit model with NaN handling
        X = sm.add_constant(X, has_constant="add")
        self.model = sm.GLM(y, X, family=sm.families.Binomial()).fit(tol=1e-12, maxiter=100)
        self.coef_ = self.model.params

        return self

    def score(self, frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        Xs = pd.DataFrame(index=frame.index)
        for v in self.woe_tabs.keys():
            t = self.woe_tabs[v]
            Xs[f"woe_{v}"] = t["woe"].reindex(frame[v]).values  # unseen level -> NA

        # Predict
        Xs = sm.add_constant(Xs, has_constant="add")
        pd_values = self.model.predict(Xs)
        points = np.round(600 + (50 / np.log(2)) * np.log((1 - pd_values) / pd_values))
        decision = np.where(pd_values > 0.35, "DECLINE", "APPROVE")

        result = pd.DataFrame({"score": pd_values, "decision": decision}, index=frame.index)
        return result

    @property
    def coef(self) -> pd.Series | None:
        if self.coef_ is not None:
            return self.coef_
        return None
notes: QUIRK: unseen levels in WoE mapping result in NaN, matching R behavior.
